newsitem.title: UK: ED&F Man sells cocoa processing unit to Archer Daniels.
newsitem.headline: ED&F Man sells cocoa processing unit to Archer Daniels.

text.p: U.S. agribusiness giant Archer Daniels Midland Co. signed a definitive agreement to buy ED&F Man Group Plc's cocoa unit, the British company said Friday, a deal that will make ADM the world's biggest cocoa processor.
Under the agreement, Decatur, Ill.-based ADM will pay $108 million in cash and assume $115 million in debt, ED&F Man said.
The takeover, ADM's second acquisition of a cocoa processing business in six months, propels it to the top of the world cocoa processing league, leapfrogging Swiss-French giant Barry-Callebaut.
Cocoa is the raw material from which chocolate is made, though it is also used in other products, including some cosmetics.
ADM is already one of the world's biggest processors of farm crops, and analysts said the deal is further proof of its ambitions.
"It's a very aggressive move, and takes them in six months to No. 1 in the cocoa world," one cocoa analyst said.

Traders estimate ADM's global bean-grinding capacity to have jumped to 450,000 metric tons against Callebaut-Barry's 350,000 metric tons and privately owned U.S. grain trading house Cargill Inc.'s 260,000.

Traders said the purchase was the latest step in the global consolidation of the cocoa trade and had implications for the commodity, traded on exchanges in London and New York. The consolidation moves have been prompted by tight margins.

In February, ADM bought Grace Cocoa from W.R. Grace & Co. for more than $470 million, a buy that included Grace Cocoa's major Dutch processor, Cacao de Zaan, since renamed ADM Zaan and now the centre for ADM's global cocoa operations.
In the latest deal, ADM is buying five ED&F Man cocoa processing units -- two in the United States, one in Britain, one in Poland and one in Brazil.
The top three processors now control around 50 percent of total world cocoa grindings, estimated by ED&F Man at 2.69 million metric tons in the 1995/96 season.

"This is the completion of the restructuring process and if you look at the three giants in the industry, they buy and sell roughly at the same margins. Cocoa is dead as a tradable commodity," one trader said.
